newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament meets to tackle flood calamity.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament meets to tackle flood calamity.

text.p: Poland's parliament was meeting in a special session on Wednesday to rush through laws easing the flow of funds and help to areas devastated by floods.
"People are dying, and the water is taking away everything they own," lower house Speaker Jozef Zych said in a televised address to the nation late on Tuesday.
He promised parliament would quickly pass measures proposed by the government to make rescue more effective now, and to help reconstruction once the water drained away.
The floods, caused by downpours last week, have killed at least 38 people so far in Poland and brought death and destruction to the neighbouring Czech Republic.

Waters were retreating in hard-hit parts of Poland's south to reveal smashed homes, broken bridges and torn roads covered in filth. Roughly 2,200 square kilometres (1,400 square miles) remained flooded including much of the cities of Wroclaw and Opole.
People living further along the Odra fled or built sandbag walls to protect their homes as a surge of high water swept north down the river towards the German border and the sea.

On Tuesday the cabinet met to decide on submitting around two dozen new or amended laws, including a revision of the 1997 budget, to cope with a catastrophe it said had directly affected at least 50,000 to 60,000 families.
It trod a tightrope between the needs to provide maximum relief and to ensure financial stability, as Poland's zloty currency slid five percent against a basket of currencies.

"The government is trying to be responsive but it is also trying to remain responsible marcro-economically and that is how I read the package of decisions made today," International Monetary Fund representative Markus Rodlauer said.
The government proposed amending this year's budget to get an additional 2.5 billion zloty ($740 million) borrowing limit in the central bank to ensure it had enough ready money.
But Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz stressed the move would not mean pumping this amount into the economy.
The government will also seek an increase in its foreign borrowing limits to accommodate a $300 million loan from the World Bank, he said during a break in the cabinet meeting.

Largely by yanking money from other budget goals and halting capital projects, the government has already lined up 650 million zlotys for flood relief and was determined to rebuild as much as possible in the months before winter.
Among other steps, it proposed quick $600 payouts to provide essentials to all households struck by the flood and free wheat from reserves to farmers with swamped land.
The government's energy now did not prevent the opposition accusing it of delays and blunders earlier in the crisis.
"In any normal democracy, there would be a vote of no confidence in the government after actions like these," Solidarity trade union chief Maciej Jankowski said.

The prime minister's Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), the dominant coalition party, is fighting an opposition bloc led by Solidarity in September 21 elections and analysts say its actions in coming days could spell victory or defeat.
Opposition leaders said the government had not declared a state of emergency as this would have delayed the polls.
Cimoszewicz defended his administration's response, saying the onset of such heavy floods had been unforseeable and a state of emergency would unnecessary.
"I think any casual opinions about lack of action, lack of preparation...are not necessarily the truth," he said.
